content: In some cases, it may also be prescribed for other conditions, such as chest pain (angina). If you have questions about its use for your specific condition, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Acebutolol is available in capsule form and is taken orally, typically once or twice daily. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. While acebutolol helps control your condition, it does not cure it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Before starting acebutolol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Additionally, disclose if you have a history of heart, kidney, or liver disease; asthma or other lung conditions; blood vessel disorders; severe allergies; diabetes; or an overactive thyroid. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking acebutolol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that acebutolol may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate this drowsiness, so exercise caution. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking acebutolol. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Acebutolol may cause side effects. Common side effects include dizziness, lightheadedness, excessive tiredness, headache, constipation, diarrhea, upset stomach, and muscle aches. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience shortness of breath, wheezing, swelling in the feet or lower legs, or chest pain. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store acebutolol in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Your doctor may also ask you to monitor your pulse. If your pulse is abnormally fast or slow, contact your doctor. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Maintain a written list of all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, and bring this list to all medical appointments or in case of emergencies. Acebutolol is also marketed under the brand name Sectral®.
